newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia says Komi republic cannot issue bond.
newsitem.headline: Russia says Komi republic cannot issue bond.

text.p: Russia's northern Komi republic does not have the right to issue a Eurobond as the territory receives monetary assistance from the federal government, the head of the Finance Ministry's securities department said on Wednesday.
When asked whether Komi republic could issue a Eurobond, Bella Zlatkis answered: "No."
She told a news conference that according to Russian legislation only regions and territories which could manage without help from the federal budget had the right to issue Eurobonds.

On Tuesday senior Komi officials said in London that the republic planned to issue a $200 million five-year Eurobond by the end of the year. Zlatkis said only eight territories had the right to issue Eurobonds according to the 1997 budget, adding the number of such territories in 1998 was likely to be less.
She said Irkutsk region, Tatar republic, Mary El republic and Sverdlovsk region had announced plans to issue Eurobonds.
The City of Moscow, St Petersburg and Nizhny Novgorod region are also planning Eurobond issues.
